response.message: We're building an authenticated AWS app that answers questions with citations over a small synthetic document set. It uses bounded keyword retrieval, enforces each document's permissions, and runs the model on Bedrock. I've drawn it end to end. Browser → CloudFront web app (Cognito sign-in with PKCE and MFA) → API Gateway with a JWT check → Lambda, which reads only the documents you're allowed to see from the DynamoDB catalog and then calls Bedrock Converse. Ingestion is the operator tool that comes with the catalog: it loads the synthetic documents and their explicit access lists. The first local test (Outputs → Emulate locally) runs the code against simulated AWS services with scripted model replies and synthetic sign-in tokens. It shows retrieval, access filtering and citation handling, but it proves nothing about real model quality, IAM, sign-in or deployment. Checking the real model needs an approved Bedrock model ID, model access and quotas in your own account, and nothing here is deployed or verified. Which country does this data need to stay in? That decides which AWS region and Bedrock model we can propose.

proposal.title: Bounded keyword RAG on AWS with an authenticated web app
proposal.body: Scope: a citation-backed question-answering app over a synthetic collection of up to 100 small UTF-8 documents. Flow: browser (existing client) → CloudFront web app → Cognito (PKCE, MFA) → API Gateway JWT route → Lambda keyword retrieval → DynamoDB catalog with explicit ACLs → Bedrock Converse. Ingestion uses the catalog's generated operator management tool. Assumptions: region, country and Bedrock model ID are not decided yet; model access and quotas are unverified; this is keyword retrieval, not vector search. Nothing has been deployed.

data.label: User browser
data.description: Existing client reference for a signed-in user. Not provisioned.

data.label: RAG web app
data.description: Hosts the browser app from private S3 assets behind CloudFront access control. Signs users in with authorization code + PKCE, then calls the API with an access token and shows answers with citations.

data.label: User pool
data.description: Admin-created users with required software-token MFA. Issues scoped access tokens. Identity-to-employee-region mappings live in the catalog. Users are onboarded through the generated operator tool; no passwords are stored in the diagram.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: Bounded authenticated HTTP API with a JWT browser route. Unknown identities fail closed. No anonymous access.

data.label: Keyword retrieval and answer
data.description: Runs keyword search over the catalog, filters by the caller's ACL and region, rechecks document revisions, calls the model and returns a cited answer, or abstains when nothing grounds it. Owns its execution role, logs, version and alias.

data.label: Document catalog and ACLs
data.description: Up to 100 small synthetic UTF-8 documents with explicit per-document ACLs and identity mappings. Ingestion: an operator loads documents through the generated conditional management tool. Caller roles cannot write to it.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: A direct foundation model reached through Converse. The model ID, model access, quotas and regional availability are still unselected and unverified. Locally, model replies are mocked.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If permissions leak, people can see content they shouldn't. This is the main thing the qualification needs to prove.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "keep all source permissions" and "identity enforcement".
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: answers may only use documents the signed-in user is allowed to read. If the user's identity is unknown, the request is refused.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without citations, nobody can check an answer, and unsupported answers erode trust.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Answer questions over a small synthetic document collection with citations".
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: every answer cites the documents it came from. If no permitted document supports an answer, the app abstains.

requirementDrafts.rationale: A mock can't show answer quality or prove that the model is available.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation".
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: keep mocked local model results separate from real Bedrock validation. Real validation needs an approved model ID, model access and quotas in the chosen region.

response.message: Good news: the local emulation of revision 2 passed with no failures or gaps. That means the generated code ran correctly against simulated AWS services for retrieval, permission filtering and cited answers. It doesn't verify real sign-in, IAM, API routing, Bedrock answer quality or deployment, so we don't need a diagram change. What matters most now is the boundary we haven't tested, and the region depends on where the data is allowed to live. Which country does this synthetic data need to stay in? With that, we can propose an AWS region and check which Bedrock model is available there for a real validation.
